TAJBank Limited, Nigeria’s largest non-interest bank, has, for the fifth consecutive time, won the Non-Interest Bank of the Year Award at the BusinessDay Media Limited’s Banks and Other Financial Institutions Awards 2026. The Founder and Managing Director of TAJBank, Mr. Hamid Joda, said the recognition reinforced the bank’s responsibility to widen access to non-interest banking and deliver transparent and customer-focused financial services that meet the needs of individuals, businesses and underserved communities. Mr Joda, according to a statement issued at the weekend by the bank’s Head of Marketing Communications, Isiaka Wakili, thanked the management of BusinessDay Media Ltd for recognising TAJBank’s contributions to the nation’s non-interest banking industry. “We are deeply honoured to receive the Non-Interest Bank of the Year Award at the 2026 BAFI Awards. This recognition belongs to our Board of Directors, management, dedicated staff and most importantly, our valued customers, whose confidence continues to inspire us. “We see this award not merely as a celebration of our achievements, but as a renewed call to deepen financial inclusion, strengthen our commitment to ethical banking and develop innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers,” Joda said. He said the award would spur the bank to consolidate its gains, explore new growth opportunities and deliver greater value to customers while reinforcing its position in the nation’s non-interest banking sector. The Publisher/CEO of BusinessDay Media Ltd, Frank Aigbogun, in a statement, noted that “to be recognised as Non-Interest Bank of the Year “is to be acknowledged as an institution demonstrating that banking can simultaneously deliver profitability, trust, and responsible financial stewardship.” Aigbogun said in a financial landscape increasingly shaped by questions of sustainability, ethics and long-term trust, TAJBank had distinguished itself as one of Nigeria’s most dynamic and credible non-interest financial institutions.
